summary: Code review FAIL — one Blocking bug found in publish-locations.js.

The getPublishLocations() function was extended to include a third entry for 'Claude Code skills' (~/.claude/skills/). This function is the sole source consumed by cmdCleanAgents in cli.js. As a result, running 'clean-agents' (or 'clean-agents --force') now inadvertently lists and deletes all .md files from ~/.claude/skills/, including the freshly-published skill files — this is beyond the intended scope of clean-agents, which was designed to clean persona files only.

All other aspects of the implementation are well-structured: readBuiltFiles/deploySkill decomposition is clean, error collection pattern is correct, cross-platform path handling is proper (path.join throughout), CLI integration mirrors existing conventions, and the stem-scoped rmSync ensures hand-written sibling directories are untouched.

comments.note: BLOCKING — scripts/publish-locations.js getPublishLocations(): The third entry '{ label: "Claude Code skills", dir: getClaudeCodeSkillsDir(), filter: f => f.endsWith(".md") }' must be REMOVED from this function. The function is documented as a 'Single source of truth for persona publish locations' and is consumed exclusively by cmdCleanAgents in cli.js. Adding the skills directory here means 'clean-agents --force' will delete all .md files from ~/.claude/skills/, destroying published skill files. Fix: remove the skills entry from the array. The getClaudeCodeSkillsDir() helper export can remain — it is correctly used directly by publish-skills.js and sync-personas.js.

No action required — all other implementation dimensions pass. publish-skills.js structure (readBuiltFiles/deploySkill decomposition, error accumulation, stem-scoped rmSync to protect sibling dirs) is clean and correct. build-skills.js correctly uses a separate TargetRegistry to avoid polluting defaultRegistry. CLI commands in cli.js are consistent with existing patterns.
